cohort: Preterm neonates with gestational age 26-37 weeks who needed ventilation support and were admitted to the neonatal care unit at Misan Hospital for Child and Maternity during 2018
finding: The study found a high rate of preterm admission (36.1% mortality) and identified various risk factors for mortality including lower gestational age, lower anthropometric parameters, vaginal delivery, need for ventilation support, low maternal education, rural setting, fewer antenatal visits, antepartum hemorrhage, previous abortions, and premature rupture of membrane.
mod_finding: Preterm mortality was more significant in those who delivered vaginally.
